data.body: `AWS_REGION`/`AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` (and `aws-region` a few lines above) are populated from `${{ inputs['region'] }}` with no fallback, even though this new input is `required: false` with a schema `default: us-west-2`. Every other place this PR adds the same `region` input — `codex-issue-worker.yml`, `issue-triage.yml`, `notify.yml`, and the three entry workflows (`ai-issue-implementation.yml`, `ai-pr-review-address.yml`, `ai-pr-review.yml`) — defensively uses `${{ inputs['region'] || 'us-west-2' }}` for the identical purpose. `codex-review.yml` is a standalone public reusable workflow (`uses: ./.github/workflows/codex-review.yml` is also reachable by external callers independent of `ai-pr-review.yml`); if a caller explicitly passes an empty string for `region` (bypassing the schema default, which only applies when the input is omitted), `aws-region` becomes empty and `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` fails with an unrelated-looking region error instead of the clear `::error::` validation that `model` and `reasoning-effort` get in the same job. Add the same `|| 'us-west-2'` fallback used elsewhere in this PR (and ideally validate the region format alongside `model`/`reasoning-effort` in the existing `review-config` step) for consistency and defense-in-depth.
